Helen Wills Moody. An American tennis champion of the 1920s and 1930s who won nineteen Grand Slam singles titles, dominating the era and establishing herself as one of the sport's greatest players. Her technical mastery, powerful game, and graceful demeanor made her an international icon and a pioneering female athlete of her generation. She won one Australian Open, four French Opens, eight Wimbledons, and six US Opens for a total of nineteen major championships. She won nine consecutive Wimbledon matches between 1927 and 1938 without losing, and nineteen consecutive US Open matches, establishing records of dominance that stood for decades. Known as "Little Miss Poker Face" for her calm demeanor and emotional control on court, her technical mastery and reliable baseline game set the standard for her era. She reached world number one in 1927, during an era before formal ranking systems tracked rankings precisely, but she was universally acknowledged as the best player in the world. She maintained her supremacy for over a decade of competition. She won all the major tournaments across hard, clay, and grass surfaces, demonstrating exceptional versatility for her time. She married tennis player Frederick Moody in 1929 and later Edmund Leach, and her name evolved through her marriages, complicating the recognition and consistency of her record in later eras.
